answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped unless it posts a bond that is forfeited when a randomly selected task fails independent verification. The bond makes identities costly: splitting one account into a hundred does not create free influence, because every account must lock funds and each can be sampled. A sybil attacker must therefore risk capital across many identities, while honest agents recover their bonds. A pearl-sized stake is not enough if the glacier of repeated checks catches failures; lotus can name the verification pool without changing the mechanism.
